newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends up in reduced volume.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends up in reduced volume.

text.p: Shanghai's B shares index closed up on Monday after last week's falls, but trading volume decreased with overseas investors leaving the market ahead of the Christmas holiday, brokers said.
The index rose 0.944 points or 1.48 percent to 64.678 points on volume of 17.2 million shares worth $8.1 million.
The B index lost 3.84 percent last week on volatile trading after Beijing launched a crackdown on the stock markets.
Brokers said had sentiment stabilised with the crackdown shock nearly over, and trading was slow with the holiday drawing near.
All 42 B shares traded, with 27 up, six flat and nine down.
"With market fundamentals improving, most investors did not want to sell their shares at current low prices and long-term investors started building positions," one broker said.
"The index is likely to rise above the 65-point resistance level tomorrow, which would trigger follow-up buying," a second broker said.
Sanmao Textile was the star on a technical rebound, jumping $0.018 or 9.27 percent to $0.212, on volume of 29,000 shares.
Shangling Electric Appliances was the second best performer, rising $0.030 or 7.94 percent to $0.408, on volume of 34,000 shares.
Real estate developer Lujiazui traded the most on inter-institutional trading, gaining $0.020 or 1.67 percent to $1.220, on volume of 2.1 million shares.
Shanghai A share rose on a technical rebound after sharp falls in the past week, but market sentiment remained cautious with limited follow-up buying after last week's crackdown, brokers said.

The A index closed up 17.606 points or 1.91 percent to 939.946 points, on volume of 404.0 million shares worth 3.5 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index rose 25.952 points or 1.08 percent to 2431.699 points.
Hebei Weiyuan Industry was the star on institutional buying ahead of the close, soaring 0.45 yuan or 10 percent to 4.93 yuan, on volume of 3.6 million shares.
